what_it_does: Modern CPUs can develop microscopic defects in their silicon that cause them to silently produce wrong answers without triggering any alarm — a phenomenon called Silent Data Corruption (SDC). In large data centers with millions of servers, even a tiny per-chip SDC rate causes a steady stream of mysterious application failures: crashes, corrupted results, strange log messages. Attributing these failures to a specific faulty CPU is hard because the same crash signature can arise from software bugs or from hardware defects on many different chips. Hardware Sentinel is a framework that correlates software-level failure signals (crashes, segmentation faults, application logs) with hardware identity information across an entire fleet of servers, building statistical models that link failure patterns to specific CPU types or units. It was validated against six years of real failure data across 13 applications and 27 data center regions.
